To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

mice with selective deletion in the B splice variant of the Na,K-2Cl co- transporter (NKCC2) show normal salt balance but a reduced sensitivity of tubuloglomer- ular feedback and a slightly reduced loop of Henle salt re- absorption, which is due to an increased distal Cl concentration.

mice with a specific deletion of the B variant of the NKCC2 show a mild phenotype, with reduced sensitivity of tubuloglomerul feedback function and a reduced plasma renin concentration in the high salt intake state.

mice with a selective deletion of the splice variant NKCC2B do not display a salt-wasting phenotype but show a slightly reduced loop of Henle NaCl absorption, a reduced macula densa sensitivity for tubuloglomerlular feedback, and reduced plasma renin concentration under conditions of salt excess.

the B isoform contributes to salt reabsorption in the loop of Henel, but it is not essential for salt reabsorption or for the maintenance of normal blood pressure.

the NKCC2A isoform is essential for salt absorption in the thick ascending loop of Henle and the NKCC2F isoform for salt absorption in both the thin ascending limb of Henles loop and the distal convoluted tubule, but the NKCC2 isoform has a minor role for salt absorption in these segments.
the NKCC2 splice variants are differentially expressed along the nephron, but their functional significance remains to be determined.
